1av is fixed at firmware/src/usb_pump.c:153-155 by a tud_mount_cb override re-issuing tud_sof_cb_enable(true), with a comment recording exactly why the boot-time call in main.c did not survive: usbd.c:793's process_set_config calls configuration_reset, which tu_varclr()s the whole _usbd_dev struct including the sof_consumer bitfield, and that runs on every bus reset and every SET_CONFIGURATION. tud_mount_cb fires at usbd.c:809, strictly after, so it is the first point where the enable sticks. The comment also establishes why no tud_umount_cb or tud_resume_cb re-arm is needed -- SET_INTERFACE does not call configuration_reset, so sof_consumer survives alt-set changes, and a real bus reset always culminates in a fresh SET_CONFIGURATION and therefore a fresh mount. Confirmed on hardware during the okx soak: sof_isr climbs at 1000/s where it previously read 0 for an entire capture.

Merged to main at 1232b48. Merged to main at dc044fc. Firmware cross-compiles to a 1169920-byte uf2, zero build artifacts tracked. Three parts, all reviewed and APPROVED.

PART A, sqrt to sqrtf at sigana_ldac.c:44,53,61,66 -- 256 calls per frame across both channels. V0 PASSED ON HARDWARE, offline, no Bluetooth: HQ mean 1198 to 1064us, minus 134us or 11.2 percent, against a gate of 80us. SQ 1178 to 1038, MQ 1158 to 1007. nm confirms __aeabi_f2d, __aeabi_d2f and sqrt are gone from the built object, re-derived independently by the reviewer rather than read off a claim.

THE CORRECTNESS QUESTION I ASKED WAS ANSWERED PROPERLY, and it was the one that mattered: does a faster encoder quietly change what we transmit? No. struct_ldac.h:50 typedefs SCALAR as float unconditionally in this build, so the operand at all four sites was ALREADY float -- the old code promoted float to double, took a double sqrt, and truncated back. The new code takes a correctly-rounded sqrtf directly. Both are correctly rounded to the nearest representable float, so the difference is bounded at about 1 ULP in single precision, far below the encoder's own thresholds such as LDAC_TH_LOWENERGY_L at 225.47. Bit allocation is unaffected. Ruled out by reading, not asserted.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN PREMISE, worth keeping: it assumed a newlib softfloat bit-loop. It was not. pico_link.elf.map:14906 resolves sqrt to __wrap_sqrt in pico-sdk's pico_double/double_aeabi_dcp.S, the RP2350 double coprocessor. The saving is real but smaller than a softfloat assumption would predict, which is why 11.2 percent and not more.

PART B, the stop_dwell WARNING. Edge-triggered on an actual rise via s_last_stop_dwell, reached only inside pl_a2dp_report in THREAD context from main.c:558 under the shared 1-second report clock. No IRQ risk and no flood risk at worst one line per second, which matters because the console already drops over 16 million bytes under load. This is the warning whose absence let a counter print the answer all session unnoticed.

PART C, two false claims corrected. libldac/CMakeLists.txt:14-17 and PROVENANCE.md's Arithmetic mode section both asserted the default float path had no double-precision arithmetic; the link map disproved it. PROVENANCE.md was APPENDED to rather than overwritten -- the stale finding stays visible with a dated Fixed block beneath it and an instruction to re-verify with nm after any SDK refresh, which is the right shape for a local patch to Apache-2.0 vendored code.

THE MOST IMPORTANT OUTCOME IS THE BENCH FIX. ldac_bench.c re-encoded ONE identical 128-sample two-tone block 200 times, converging bit allocation, frmana_cnt and the MDCT overlap to a fixed point real music never reaches. That is why it reported EQMID-independent timing all session. With a genuinely continuous non-repeating sweep -- frequency and amplitude modulated by slow sinusoids over a running cursor that never resets, including across EQMID cases -- HQ, SQ and MQ now show REAL SEPARATION where the old bench showed none. It also reports p50/p95/p99, because the dwell cap reads a SUM and the mean was the wrong statistic.

That vindicates Andreas's ear over the instrument: he heard MQ as clearly better than HQ while the bench insisted they cost the same. The instrument was wrong. Recorded because the general lesson is the expensive one -- a benchmark whose input never varies measures a fixed point, not the workload.
